# IDS Model Check

> Free, MIT-licensed checker for buildingSMART IDS 1.0 (Information Delivery Specification) files against IFC building models (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3; STEP .ifc, ifcXML, ifcJSON, IFC5 alpha .ifcx or .ifczip). Runs in the browser with nothing uploaded, or as a dependency-free Node command line. Exports BCF 2.1 issues, CSV, JSON and a self-contained HTML report.

- Page: https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/
- Source: https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/ids-model-check
- Accuracy: 334 of 334 of buildingSMART's IDS test pairs (suite commit 870f9c4, 2026-09-25); same verdicts and failing elements as IfcTester on five real models, except multiple xs:pattern restrictions, where it follows XSD and the suite (patterns are alternatives). IFC 4.3 infrastructure and HVAC (2026-11-17): buildingSMART's twelve Simple-Scene models (bridge, road, rail, earthworks, plumbing, ducts) with three IDS files, 348 of 348 specification results identical to IfcTester 0.8.0; on the IFC2X3 HVAC copy it also finds the IfcFlowTerminal/IfcFlowSegment occurrences typed as air terminals and ducts, which IfcTester does not (eval/infra-mep-crosscheck-2026-11-17.md). Public IDS files on real exports (2026-11-17): 65 public IDS files on four opensourceBIM exports; IfcTester 0.9.0 opened 53, and on those 1,661 of 1,736 specification results are identical; the 75 differences are IfcTester counting IFC2X3 IfcWallStandardCase typed by IfcWallType as IFCWALL (IDS has no inheritance), prohibited specifications with requirements (invalid per buildingSMART's suite) and untyped True booleans. Reports now say what an entity facet leaves out: "not checked: 101 IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE (a subclass of IFCWALL)" (skippedSubclasses in JSON), verdict unchanged; 76 PASS results on these models had left subclass elements unchecked (eval/corpus-crosscheck-2026-11-17.md). Classes outside the model's schema (2026-11-24): an IFC4X3 file that writes IFC4's IFCBEAMSTANDARDCASE (IfcOpenShell drops such records, so no tool checked its 18 beams; 7 of the 26 public specifications that reach IfcBeam passed it) now gets a reader note per class and "not checked: 18 IFCBEAMSTANDARDCASE (not in IFC4X3_ADD2; another schema's subclass of IFCBEAM)" on the specification; on IfcOpenShell's 293 test models x 65 public IDS, 125,167 of 126,781 results match IfcTester 0.9.0 and every difference has a cause already named (eval/ifcopenshell-test-files-2026-11-24.md). Starter IDS files: samples/coordination-basics.ids.xml, samples/quantities-and-naming.ids.xml, samples/infrastructure-and-mep.ids.xml (bridges, roads, rail, earthworks, ducts, pipes).

## Guides

- [How to check an IFC model against an IDS file](https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/how-to-check-an-ifc-model-against-an-ids-file.html)
- [How to write an IDS file in Excel or as a CSV](https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/how-to-write-an-ids-file-in-excel.html)
- [How to add missing property values to an IFC model](https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/how-to-add-missing-property-values-to-an-ifc-model.html)

## Use

- Browser: drop a model (.ifc, .ifcxml, ifcJSON .json, IFC5 .ifcx or .ifczip) and a .ids, read each specification's result and the failing elements, download BCF/CSV/JSON, or the HTML report (verdict, per-specification table, the requirements and IFC classes that fail most, every failing element with GlobalId and reason; one offline file that prints; `node cli.mjs model.ifc spec.ids --html report.html`).
- CLI: `node cli.mjs model.ifc|.ifcxml|.json|.ifczip spec.ids [--json] [--bcf out.bcfzip]`; exit 0 all pass, 1 a specification fails or is invalid, 2 error.
- IDS audit with no model: `node cli.mjs --audit spec.ids` (or "Audit the IDS only" on the page) reports specifications that are invalid against the IFC schema: unknown or lower-case classes, attributes a class lacks or has only as derived/inverse, values compared with lists/objects/selects, malformed numbers, integers and booleans, patterns on numbers, unknown dataTypes, prohibited specifications with requirements; standard property and quantity sets against buildingSMART's templates for IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3 ADD2 (Pset_/Qto_ names and properties the standard lacks, with the nearest standard name; a dataType the template does not give; a set the selected classes cannot carry), as buildingSMART's IDS-Audit-tool does; and (2026-11-19, warning pset-predefined) a set the IFC4/IFC4X3 templates give only some predefined types (Pset_ActuatorTypeElectricActuator: IfcActuator/ELECTRICACTUATOR) required with no predefinedType or another one; the editor labels such sets, fills in the type and hides them once another type is chosen (1,008 of 1,008 limited editor offers agree with the audit, eval/predefined-sets-2026-11-19.md). Template types (2026-11-19, warnings pset-occurrence and pset-performance): an occurrence set (PSET_/QTO_OCCURRENCEDRIVEN, Pset_FanOccurrence) required on a type object such as IFCFANTYPE, and a performance history set (PSET_PERFORMANCEDRIVEN, Pset_FanPHistory) required on the element instead of the IfcPerformanceHistory that carries it; requiring a performance set on IFCPERFORMANCEHISTORY is no longer a false pset-class error. The editor stops offering occurrence sets on type objects and offers performance sets on IFCPERFORMANCEHISTORY; all 1,280 class/set pairs it offered before agree with the audit (eval/template-types-2026-11-19.md). Also checks the file's structure against ids.xsd (structure.mjs: element order, allowed attributes, cardinality/relation/ifcVersion/dataType values, <simpleValue> or <xs:restriction>, XSD 1.0 facets, the root namespace), with the line of each fault: same verdict as IfcTester's ids.xsd validation on 145 of 145 public and IDS-Audit-tool files and 2,935 of 2,935 mutated copies; 12 of 65 public IDS files break it (IDS 0.9's minOccurs on <specification>, the schema URL as namespace, ifcVersion IFC4X3); a model check still runs such a specification, with a warning (eval/ids-structure-2026-11-18.md). Repair (2026-11-18, fix.mjs; page "Download repaired IDS" after an audit, `node cli.mjs --fix spec.ids -o out.ids`): edits the file's own text for the faults with one right answer (IDS 0.9 minOccurs on <specification> moved to <applicability> and to cardinality on facets, property <name>/datatype to <baseName>/dataType, IFC4X3 to IFC4X3_ADD2, the schema URL as namespace, bare text wrapped in <simpleValue>, schema order, a bare &); files with no fault come back byte for byte (682 of 682), the checker reads the same specifications from every repaired copy (217 of 217), 198 of 217 then valid in IfcTester's ids.xsd; 6 of the 12 failing public files come back valid. The reader now reads those IDS 0.9 forms as written rather than as "anything" (48 facets in 8 public files) (eval/fix-structure-2026-11-18.md). Flags 26 of buildingSMART's 27 invalid IDS test files and none of the 307 valid ones, and all 5 property set files in the IDS-Audit-tool's invalid set. A model check still runs a specification whose only fault is a property set template one, with a warning. An entity facet (applicability or partOf) naming an abstract class such as IFC2X3's IFCBUILDINGELEMENT gets a class-abstract warning naming the concrete classes below it: IDS matches exact classes, so it selects nothing; 2 of 64 public IDS files (RVB BIM Norm v1.1), 0 of 954 buildingSMART and IDS-Audit-tool specifications (eval/abstract-classes-2026-11-17.md).
- IFC to COBie 2.4, and COBie QC (https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/cobie.html; CLI `node cli.mjs --cobie MODEL.ifc -o OUT.xlsx [--from-geometry] [--stage design|handover] [--contact "EMAIL,COMPANY,PHONE"]` and `node cli.mjs --cobie-qc WORKBOOK.xlsx|CSV-DIR`, exit 1 when the QC finds errors; cobie.mjs): the nine NBIMS-US COBie 2.4 sheets from the model, maintainable products only as Components, values left blank (never invented) when the model lacks them; --from-geometry places components the file leaves on a storey in the room their body stands in (doors and windows: both sides) with ifc-quantity-takeoff; the QC checks required cells by stage, template placeholders (a cell holding its own column name), duplicate keys, references, emails, ISO dates, numbers and pick lists. 25 public exports written; 791 of 869 doors and windows get exactly the rooms the file's own space boundaries name, 19 a room it does not; 935 of 1,227 components a file puts in a room placed there with the containment hidden, 89 elsewhere (eval/cobie-2026-11-23.md).
- Compare two IDS versions (https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/revision.html; CLI `node cli.mjs --diff OLD.ids NEW.ids [MODEL.ifc] [--json]`, exit 1 when the revision asks more): specifications added, removed and changed, each change graded asks more / asks less / different / metadata, patterns compared as XSD regex languages with the shortest value that matched before and not now (pattern-lang.mjs; 3,540 of 3,540 public pattern pairs decided, every example verified, eval/pattern-inclusion-2026-11-20.md; date ranges read as the exact strings the checker passes, so a date range compares with a pattern, a list or another range, and dateTime, time and duration ranges as intervals, eval/date-range-revisions-2026-11-20.md); with a model, elements newly failing (matched by GlobalId), already failing with more to fix, and no longer failing. 69 committed revisions of 27 public IDS files compared with 0 errors (eval/revision-diff-2026-11-20.md).
- IDS editor (https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/editor.html): build an IDS 1.0 file by picking an IFC class, a standard Pset_/Qto_ set that class can carry (its own, an ancestor's, or for a type object its occurrence's, except occurrence-only sets; performance history sets on IFCPERFORMANCEHISTORY) and a property; writes the template's dataType, offers the standard enumeration values, lists subclasses (IDS matches exact classes), audits live, downloads the .ids or sends it to the checker. Every offered class/set/property (203,433 specifications over IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3) audits with no error or warning (measured 2026-11-16; since 2026-11-19 a set the templates give only some predefined types draws pset-predefined until the type is set, which the editor fills in for one-type sets, eval/predefined-sets-2026-11-19.md); a 15,102-specification sample validates against ids.xsd in IfcTester. Opens an existing IDS (importIds): editable rows where the page can hold a facet unchanged, the rest kept as written; 64 of 64 public IDS files, 12 of 12 IDS-Audit-tool valid files and 187 of 187 buildingSMART pass cases write back asking the same, none made invalid against ids.xsd (eval/editor-open-2026-11-16.md). Opening repairs first (2026-11-18, repairOnOpen): the one-answer ids.xsd faults and foreign-regex patterns fix.mjs repairs are fixed as the file opens and listed; public files written back valid with no pattern finding 55 to 60 of 65, pattern findings in written-back files 9 to 0 (eval/editor-open-repair-2026-11-18.md). Open a model to write for (inventory.mjs modelInventory, run in worker.mjs): lists the model's classes with counts and the sets their objects carry, offers the carried standard sets first and the model's own sets (any name outside the case-sensitive Pset_/Qto_ prefixes, e.g. Revit's PSet_Revit_Dimensions) as editable rows with the data type the model writes; on 4 real exports 347 of 395 (class, set) pairs were own sets and 21 of 122 standard properties used a data type the template does not give (eval/model-inventory-2026-11-16.md). Several classes per specification (2026-11-17): an "Also applies to" list written as one entity facet; the page offers only the sets, attributes and predefined types every class shares (commonSets, commonAttributes, commonPredefinedTypes); 29 class-list specifications in 11 public IDS files now open as editable, 81.1% of public facets editable (was 79.4%), all still writing back the same (eval/several-classes-2026-11-17.md). A subclass box per class (2026-11-18): each further class has its own "and its subclasses" box, and an opened list naming a class with all its concrete subclasses opens with it ticked (classListBases); public files list 368 names where they listed 506, all writing back the same (eval/also-subclasses-2026-11-18.md). Deprecated subclasses (2026-11-19, boxSubclasses): in IFC4X3 a ticked box leaves out IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE and IFCELECTRICDISTRIBUTIONBOARD, which IFC 4.3 deprecates, and names them; 0 in 57 public IFC4X3 exports, so the bSDD templates open as 30 classes (was 79) (eval/deprecated-subclasses-2026-11-19.md). A model's values (2026-11-17): each property row lists the values the open model holds (inventory.mjs reads them with the checker's PropertyFacet.values, SI units) and offers "Allow exactly these values" (one-of) or "Use the model's range"; range bounds are rounded outward (outwardBound) because IDS ranges take no tolerance, and on 4 real exports 364 of 752 ranges from values as displayed failed their own model while all 1,014 requirements built from the offers pass; "one of" works on any text property or attribute, 82.0% of public facets editable (eval/model-values-2026-11-17.md). Attribute values and classification codes (2026-11-17): attribute rows (Name, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType) and classification rows offer the model's values and each system's codes (modelAttributes, modelCodes); on 4 real exports all 242 attribute one-of offers with no empty value pass their model; objects classified in a system with an empty code (143 of 210 Uniformat-classified elements and 93 of 134 type objects in the Schultz Residence Revit export) are counted, and "Require a code" writes a .+ pattern that fails exactly them (eval/model-attr-codes-2026-11-17.md). Conditions beyond the class (2026-11-17): "Narrow it" adds property, attribute, classification, material or place rows to a specification's applicability (written with no cardinality); with a model open each says how many of the class's objects it keeps (appMatchCount, equal to the checker's applicable count on 11 tested conditions, null where the inventory cannot tell); opened files' applicability facets open as rows when they write back unchanged: 83.5% of public facets editable (was 82.0%), IDS-Audit-tool valid files 21.5% (was 9.7%) (eval/applicability-rows-2026-11-17.md). Numeric attribute ranges (2026-11-17): real and integer attributes (OverallHeight, Elevation, NumberOfRiser) get a "between" mode and "Use the model's range", written with an xs:double or xs:integer base; boolean attributes are asked true/false (attributeValueKind); on 4 real exports and the sample house 27 of 27 numeric and 6 of 6 boolean requirements built from the model pass it, same verdict as IfcTester on all 33; attributes are compared in the model's own units, not SI, in this checker and in IfcTester (eval/model-attr-ranges-2026-11-17.md). Values with no dataType (2026-11-17): an opened property value with no dataType becomes an editable row that writes none (typeRow adds the template's type on request); 84.9% of public facets editable (was 83.6%); a standard boolean written TRUE with no dataType matched 0 sample walls in this checker and 2 in IfcTester 0.8.0, so the row and the audit warn (eval/untyped-values-2026-11-17.md). Accept any data type (2026-11-17, untypeRow): a standard-set row whose open model writes the property in another type (Reference as IFCLABEL, not IFCIDENTIFIER) can drop its dataType; on 2 real exports 791 of 966 objects failed only for their type, none do with no dataType, audit clean, same verdict as IfcTester 0.8.0 on 21 of 21; real-number values stay presence-only because checkers read them apart (eval/model-any-type-2026-11-17.md). A project's own property written in two data types (2026-11-24, mixedModelTypes, untypeOwnRow): the row gives the count per type (ARK_NUS's Constraints.Level: IFCLABEL on 162 rooms, IFCTEXT on 145) and offers Accept any data type, which keeps the value when every type is text; on 28 engine_web-ifc public exports offers built from the model went from 19,296 to 19,300 of 19,300 passing their model, same verdict as IfcTester 0.9.0 on 8 of 8 (eval/mixed-type-own-props-2026-11-24.md). Exporter infinity and NaN (2026-11-24): 1.#INF, -1.#IND, 1.#QNAN in a STEP file are read as Infinity/NaN with a reader note instead of dropping the record (a property holding one had gone missing, so an optional check passed it); checks fail them and the editor lists them as INF/NaN, outside the model's range; xBIM's 128 test files all read, 3,786 of 3,786 offers pass, 24,290 of 24,290 strings match IfcOpenShell 0.9.0 (eval/xbim-test-files-2026-11-24.md). Date, time and duration ranges (2026-11-17): IFCDATE, IFCDATETIME, IFCTIME and IFCDURATION rows get a between mode written on xs:date, xs:dateTime, xs:time or xs:duration (IDS 1.0 DataTypes); IfcTester 0.9.0 casts range bounds to float and fails every object on them (0 of 10 date ranges agree on 61 doors), so the row warns and "Write as a pattern" (datePattern) rewrites a date range as the XSD pattern of the same dates, read the same by both (10 of 10, same failing doors; exact since 2026-11-20: only days that exist, ASCII digits, zones placed by their instant, 0 of 310 door verdicts unlike the range vs 50 for the old shape, eval/date-pattern-exact-2026-11-20.md; dateTime ranges too since 2026-11-21 (dateTimePattern: exact on the whole fraction since the checker orders it as XSD does (temporalCompare), 24:00:00, the 44 UTC offsets in use; 0 of 290 beam verdicts unlike the range, IfcTester 10 of 10, eval/datetime-pattern-2026-11-21.md); time ranges too since 2026-11-21 (timePattern; a time of 24:00:00 is 00:00:00 as in XSD; 0 of 300 work-schedule verdicts unlike the range, IfcTester 10 of 10, eval/time-pattern-2026-11-21.md)); presence-only standard properties with no dataType open as rows, 86.4% of public facets editable (eval/date-ranges-2026-11-17.md). The model's range on dates (2026-11-17): with a model open, date, date-time, time and duration rows offer "Use the model's range", the earliest and latest of every value the model holds (inventory.mjs tmin/tmax, not only the 50 listed), merged across classes, none when any value has another form; on 600 generated doors the range and its pattern pass the model and fail a door one day late, driven in Chromium (eval/model-date-range-2026-11-17.md). One-of rows on dates and durations (2026-11-17): written on xs:date, xs:dateTime, xs:time or xs:duration like ranges; an opened list on xs:string keeps it so earlier files write back unchanged; both this checker and IfcTester compare listed values as text whatever the base (8 rows on 61 doors: same failing doors on both bases, 16 of 16 the same in IfcTester 0.9.0); 13 more IDS-Audit-tool facets editable (eval/date-oneof-2026-11-17.md). Specifications with no class (2026-11-17): a specification selected by an attribute or property alone offers every standard set and every attribute some class has (468 in IFC4), typed only when every class types it the same; IDS-Audit-tool valid files 75.9% of facets editable (was 28.1%), public files 89.2% (was 86.4%), all still writing back the same (eval/no-class-specs-2026-11-17.md). One-of rows on numbers (2026-11-17): number properties and attributes take a one-of list on xs:double or xs:integer (numberValueProblem refuses values IDS cannot read); "Allow exactly these values" from an open model (at most 12 values) lists each number exactly as held (inventory.mjs exact), because IfcTester 0.9.0 compares listed numbers with no tolerance while this checker uses IDS's; on 4 real exports 663 of 663 offered lists pass their model, IfcTester agrees on 646 (17 apart are feet/degree conversions) and on only 22 of 324 lists typed to 6 digits; IDS-Audit-tool valid files 89.2% of facets editable (was 75.9%) (eval/number-oneof-2026-11-17.md). Specifications written for several IFC versions (ifcVersion="IFC2X3 IFC4", 2026-11-17): the file opens in the schema where most facets are editable and the page audits each specification in every schema it names, as the CLI does; on 18 public files errors the page raised and the CLI did not went from 18 to 0 (eval/multi-version-2026-11-17.md). A standard property in the file's own dataType (2026-11-17): an opened Pset_/Qto_ property in a type the template does not give (SerialNumber as IFCTEXT, GrossFloorArea as IFCREAL) opens as a row keeping it, and "Use the template's type" (templateTypeRow) fixes the audit's pset-datatype error with the value carried over; 16 rows in 7 public files, 14 errors to 0, 90.8% of public facets editable (eval/template-type-2026-11-17.md). Did you mean (2026-11-17): a property one slip from its template's name (Lenght, AkousticRating) shows the audit's "did you mean" with a "Use Length" button (nameSuggestion, renameSuggestion, renameRow); the audit counts a swapped letter pair as one slip; 17 rows in 7 public files, all editable after the fix, name errors 31 to 14 (eval/name-suggestion-2026-11-17.md). Numbers with no class named (2026-11-17): an attribute derived on a subclass (CoordinateSpaceDimension and Precision on IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext) is still a number row, noting that class's objects never hold a value; a file's xs:integer on an IfcCountMeasure (BarCount, CountValue) is kept; a value on an attribute that is a list on every class (TexCoordsList, DayComponent) stays held and the audit warns that every object it checks fails; 117 of 129 numeric lists in the IDS-Audit-tool valid files open as rows (was 109), 90.7% of their facets editable (eval/no-class-numbers-2026-11-17.md). Logic in editor.mjs (setsFor, appMatchCount, typeRow, untypeRow, templateTypeRow, propertiesOf, modelSets, modelValueOffer, outwardBound, specClassNames, buildIds, importIds).
- CI: `action.yml` (GitHub composite action: `uses: Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo/ventures/ids-model-check@main` with `models` and `ids` globs) or `node ci-cli.mjs --models GLOB --ids GLOB --junit report.xml` anywhere: every model against every IDS (or `--pairing name`), JUnit XML, Markdown job summary, GitHub annotations on the failing element's STEP line, BCF per failing pair; required/prohibited failures fail the build, optional ones are warnings (`--fail-on error|warning|never`); elements an entity facet leaves out because it names a parent class (IFCWALL, not IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE: IDS has no inheritance) are a warning in every output and the `not-checked` count, a failure with `--fail-on-unchecked`; IDS audit warnings (an abstract class like IFCBUILDINGELEMENT that selects nothing, a value with no dataType, a non-standard Pset_ property) are annotated on the IDS file at that `<specification>` line, once per IDS file, counted in `audit-warnings`, a failure with `--fail-on-audit-warnings` (on 64 public IDS files: 507 of 507 specification lines placed, 72 specifications warned). Each model and IDS is parsed once for all its pairs; each specification keeps its first 1000 failing elements (`--max-failures N`, counts exact); a truncated file fails its own pairs instead of hanging. `--gitlab-codequality FILE` writes a GitLab Code Quality report: one issue per failing element on its STEP line, fingerprinted by GlobalId and class (not #id), so a merge request's widget shows which elements it broke or fixed; on the HHS Office revisions it showed exactly the 18 real changes and 0 for a re-serialisation that renumbers every entity (an #id key would show 8,975 new and 8,975 fixed). `node cli.mjs model.ifc spec.ids --junit out.xml` for one pair.
- Schema conformance (2026-11-24, conformance.mjs; CLI `node cli.mjs --conformance model.ifc [--json]`, and a model warning on every check of a STEP file up to 40 MB): attribute counts, `*`/`$` slots, typed values in selects, wrong literal kinds, enumeration values, NaN, list sizes, references to missing or wrong-class records, abstract records, header shapes, IfcApplication UNIQUE rules, inverse counts, and (2026-11-24, where-rules.mjs) every WHERE rule of the schema (363 IFC2X3, 677 IFC4, 777 IFC4X3) run by an EXPRESS interpreter from the buildingSMART .exp text, e.g. USERDEFINED with no ObjectType, a wall typed by a door type, two psets of one name; 26,013 rule failures found by both it and ifcopenshell.validate(express_rules=True) on the same records of 492 public files, eval/where-rules-2026-11-24.md; `--no-rules` skips them (2026-11-24: every bounded INVERSE, e.g. an opening that voids nothing, a layer listed twice in one set, a pset on 169 IFC2X3 types; eval/inverse-counts-2026-11-24.md). 25 of 25 of IfcOpenShell's labelled broken files flagged, 0 of 13 good ones; same files and records flagged as ifcopenshell.validate on 492 public files, all 1,085 inverse lines included (eval/conformance-2026-11-24.md). It warns; the IDS verdict is unchanged. A failing IDS row whose element (or its type, or a property set on either) breaks CorrectPredefinedType, CorrectTypeAssigned, UniquePropertySetNames or UniquePropertyNames carries a note naming the rule (2026-11-24, markModelRules; JSON modelRules). Seeded faults (2026-11-24, eval/where-rules-seeded.mjs): 8 families, 358 seeds in 24 public files, each rule firing on exactly the seeded record (eval/where-rules-seeded-2026-11-24.md). Global RULEs and less direct rules seeded too (2026-11-24): 15 families, 1,283 seeds in 102 public files, all clean (eval/where-rules-global-seeds-2026-11-24.md). IFC2X3 and IFC4 schemas compare a placement's origin with itself in IfcSameAxis2Placement, so their IfcRepresentationContextSameWCS misses contexts with different origins; conformance adds a `context-origin` note for that.
- Duplicate GlobalIds: two IfcRoot instances sharing a GlobalId (IFC rule UR1) are a model finding in every output (page, text, CSV, BCF topic, CI annotation, job summary, GitLab issue `ifc-duplicate-globalid`, Action output `duplicate-globalids`); a warning that leaves the IDS verdict alone, a failure with `--fail-on-duplicate-globalids`. Same groups as IfcOpenShell on 133 of 133 public files.
- GlobalIds shared between models: with two or more models in one CI run, a GlobalId held in more than one model is a federation warning (annotation, job summary, GitLab issue `ifc-shared-globalid`, JSON `federation`, Action output `shared-globalids`; fails with `--fail-on-shared-globalids`); two files that are one model twice are one `ifc-model-twice` finding; shared project/site/building/storey/space/grid GlobalIds of the same class are counted, not warned. On the HHS Office architect/MEP/structural set: 1 wall in two discipline files.
- Shared on purpose (2026-11-17): `--shared-globalids-allow FILE` (Action input `shared-globalids-allow`): one rule per line, a GlobalId, a class, a class and a quoted name, or `* "name"`; a shared element every holder of which matches is not counted, nor are the types and relationships that only follow it; unused rules are listed. Without a list, followers are grouped under their element ("with it:") and a relationship reusing one GlobalId for different links is named as such. Simple-Scene IFC4: 35 findings to 23, 21 with two marker rules.
- Write what the IDS asks into the model (2026-11-21, model-fill.mjs; page panel "Write the missing values into the model"; CLI `node cli.mjs --fill model.ifc spec.ids -o filled.ifc [--to-fill todo.csv] [--values todo.csv]`): after a failing check (any model format; non-STEP is written as STEP first), writes into a copy of the .ifc the property values the IDS fixes (a simpleValue or a one-item enumeration) and the values a person typed into the to-fill table's Value column (CSV; `*` as GlobalId means every listed element); a typed value the IDS would reject is refused with the reason. Writes into the element's own set of that name, or a new set and relationship; a shared set is edited only when every holder gets the same values, else copied for the elements that change; property entities are never edited; type values are overridden on the occurrence; numbers converted from SI to the model's units; untouched records byte for byte the same. The filled file is re-read and each written value tested. Quantities (2026-11-21): Qto_ requirements (or a set the element holds as IfcElementQuantity) are written as IfcQuantityLength/Area/Volume/Count/Weight/Time by the facet's data type or the Qto_ template, into the element's own quantity set or a new IfcElementQuantity; ## Covers

- Facets: entity (with predefined type), attribute, property (and quantities, material properties, predefined property sets), classification (with parent references), material (layers, profiles, constituents, lists), partOf (aggregates, groups, containment, nests, and IDS 1.0's "IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT IFCRELFILLSELEMENT": an element in an opening of another).
- Restrictions: enumeration, pattern (read as XML Schema regex, as IDS specifies and IfcTester does: "^" and "$" are plain characters, \d any Unicode digit, [a-z-[aeiou]] subtraction), min/max inclusive/exclusive, length, minLength, maxLength. Pattern audit (2026-11-18, xsdregex.mjs): an error for a pattern that is not XSD ("(?:", "*?", "{,3}"; IfcTester stops on it), warnings for anchors, needless escapes such as "\/" and a bare \w (IfcTester reads it as letters, digits, underscore); the repaired-file download rewrites them. Same verdict as elementpath on 78 of 78 corpus patterns; 4 of 65 public IDS files have a pattern that reads differently per tool (eval/xsd-regex-2026-11-18.md). A bare \w or \s (2026-11-18): IfcTester reads them as Python does (\w takes "_" and not "+", \s takes a no-break space), so the audit warns (pattern-word-class, pattern-space-class) and the repair writes the meaning you pick as a class every checker reads alike (page choice; `cli.mjs --fix --word-class letters|xsd`); 1,500 of 1,500 random patterns read the same in elementpath and here after either spelling; 4 of 65 public IDS files write -?\d{2}\s.* (eval/word-class-2026-11-18.md).
- Large models (2026-11-17): STEP arguments are read when a check first needs them and geometry's are not kept; a 219 MB federated model of seven real exports checks against the starter IDS files at a 1.0 GB peak (was 2.5 GB), identical reports, and the page finishes it under a 1 GB heap (eval/heap-200mb-2026-11-17.md).
- Specifications that apply to every entity (2026-11-17): an argument-free prefilter per facet, requirements judged before failure text, and an indexed IFC2X3 type map; 68 public and starter IDS files take 13 s on a 40 MB MEP export (was 96 s) and 111 s on the 219 MB model (was 515 s), with identical reports; that run fits a 2 GB heap, as it did before (eval/no-entity-facet-2026-11-17.md).
- Attribute facets on geometry (2026-11-18): nested lists are stepped over, not built, since an attribute test only asks whether a list is empty; 68 IDS files on a 40 MB MEP export take 8.3 s (was 13.3 s) at 646 MB RSS (was 1,024 MB); the 219 MB federated model takes 67.5 s (was 114.3 s) and now fits a 1 GB heap; reports identical (eval/attribute-any-geometry-2026-11-18.md).
- Property facets on every entity (2026-11-18): the elements reaching each property set name are indexed once per model, so a property facet costs one lookup per element and sets are read only where a name matches; 68 IDS files on the 40 MB MEP export take 4.6 s (was 7.9 s on the same machine), on the 219 MB federated model 39.4 s (was 63.1 s); reports identical (eval/psets-cache-2026-11-18.md).
- Specifications with no entity facet (2026-11-18): candidates come from the index a facet's prefilter reads (property set holders, classification, material and relationship maps, classes with a named attribute), sorted back into file order with a per-model position array, instead of a walk over every entity; on the 40 MB MEP export the 24 public specifications that take a list run 2.9x faster in applies (896 to 305 ms), on the 219 MB federated model 6.1 to 2.2 s, reports identical (eval/file-order-candidates-2026-11-18.md).
- Repeated facets across specifications and IDS files (2026-11-18): a parsed model keeps each distinct applicability's result and, for facets run over more than a quarter of the model, one byte per entity per facet verdict (at most 8 facets), both off the JS heap; on the 40 MB MEP export the 68 public and starter IDS files ran 11.4 million facet tests, 7.9 million of them repeats, and now run 3.7 million (6.3-7.0 s to 5.0-5.3 s); on the 219 MB federated model 60.4 to 43.1 s, under a 1 GB heap 92-100 to 55-57 s; reports identical; `check(..., { facetCache: false })` turns it off (eval/applies-cache-2026-11-18.md).
- Attribute value tests on every entity (2026-11-18): attribute facets that differ only in their value share one per-entity reading (attribute set, empty, or a list or reference IDS cannot compare), kept in the verdict cache's spare bits at no extra memory; 68 IDS files on the 40 MB MEP export run 190,924 full attribute tests instead of 2,851,787 and take 2.9-3.1 s (was 4.1-4.5 s); the 219 MB federated model 28.4-29.6 s (was 35.7-36.7 s), under a 1 GB heap 35.4-36.6 s (was 49.3-51.5 s); STEP strings are no longer kept as one-character chains (20 MB on the MEP export); reports identical (eval/attribute-shape-2026-11-18.md).
- A smaller record per entity (2026-11-18): STEP entities are held by number in a plain array with the file order in a 4-byte list, not a Map, and each record has three fields; heap kept after parsing a 40 MB MEP export 93 to 65 MB, the 219 MB federated model 444 to 350 MB, which now parses in a 576 MB heap (was 704 MB) and checks against the starter IDS files in 704 MB (was 832 MB); parsing 20-30% faster; reports identical (eval/entity-table-2026-11-18.md).
- The checks' own memory (2026-11-18): read argument lists are copied to their length (a list built by push keeps room for 16), repeated small values such as IFCBOOLEAN(.T.), property names and enumerations are shared frozen objects, and relationships' arguments are not kept once indexed; the 219 MB federated model parses in a 512 MB heap (was 576 MB), checks against the starter IDS files in 576 MB (was 704 MB) and against all 68 public and starter IDS files in 704 MB (was 896 MB); reports identical (eval/shared-values-2026-11-18.md).
- Property sets as one record each (2026-11-18): the first read of a property set keeps one flat list of its name and its properties' names and entities, and the arguments of sets, properties and quantities are no longer kept; what 68 public and starter IDS files add to the 219 MB federated model's heap fell from 137 to 71 MB, and the run fits a 608 MB heap (was 704 MB), at about the same speed; reports identical on five models (eval/pset-records-2026-11-18.md).
- STEP read from the file's bytes (2026-11-18): readModel returns the file's bytes and the STEP reader decodes one record at a time when its arguments are read, so the file is never one JavaScript string; the 219 MB federated model parses in a 304 MB heap (was 512 MB), checks against the starter IDS files in 352 MB (was 544 MB) and all 68 IDS files in 448 MB (was 640 MB); STEP files past V8's 536,870,888-character string limit now open (a 670 MB, 11.0-million-entity model checks in 13.9 s; main refused it); checks about 5% slower; reports identical (eval/step-bytes-2026-11-18.md).
- ifcXML read from the file's bytes (2026-11-18): the XML reader runs over the bytes and decodes each name, attribute value and text run on its own, and lazy geometry is re-read from its byte span, so an ifcXML model is never one JavaScript string; HHS MEP as ifcXML parses in a 192 MB heap (was 336 MB), the 374 MB federated ifcXML parses and checks against all 68 IDS files in 448 MB (was 800 and 832 MB); a 680 MB ifcXML past V8's string limit now checks (25.6 s; main refused it); reports identical, times unchanged within noise (eval/ifcxml-bytes-2026-11-18.md).
- Model input: STEP; ifcXML in both the IFC2X3 (ifcXML2) and IFC4 layouts, read into the same entities as STEP (xBIM's ifcXML export of 4walls1floorSite agrees with its STEP file on 2,205 of 2,205 attribute values; on buildingSMART's 41 IFC4 Annex E examples and 2 GeometryGymIFC examples, each published as both STEP and ifcXML, the verdicts on the two forms agree 129 of 129, with href references, decimal commas, flat coordinate lists and flat B-spline control-point grids (rows from the knot counts) read; string values keep their whitespace, as in STEP; read as it streams, geometry kept only as its span, so a 374 MB ifcXML checks against 68 IDS files under a 1 GB heap, eval/lazy-ifcxml-2026-11-18.md; the nested IFC4 layout, where one element holds the whole model, reads four real IFC4/IFC4X3 exports entity for entity with 2,160 of 2,160 verdicts equal to STEP's, the schema read from the root element (not from an application name such as ARCHICAD's "IFC2x3 add-on"), eval/ifc4-layout-scale-2026-11-18.md; each nested element read as it closes, entity numbers unchanged, a single-project model parsing in 96 MB of heap where it needed 160 MB, eval/nested-early-2026-11-18.md); .ifczip with deflate, stored and zip64 entries.
- IFC5 alpha .ifcx (2026-11-21, ifcx.mjs): nodes composed (later wins, inherits, null removes) into IFC4X3 objects, spatial tree (aggregates, nests for ports and alignments, containment, voids/fills), property sets (each property to the standard set whose template names it for the class, else a set named after its namespace), classifications (<ns>::class) and materials (own or on unclassed parts); layers weakest first (cli --layer). 8 STEP/IFC5 twins: class 12,115 of 12,116, partOf 1,646 of 1,648, shared properties and materials all in the same set with the same value; 47 of 47 public files read. Systems: partofsystem read as IfcRelAssignsToGroup (IDS partOf IFCRELASSIGNSTOGROUP), connectsto as IfcRelConnectsPorts, flowdirection as the port's FlowDirection, servicesfacility as IfcRelServicesBuildings; Domestic Hot Water twin: 9 of 9 members, 35 of 35 directions, 15 of 15 port pairs as in STEP (eval/ifcx-systems-2026-11-21.md).
- ifcJSON (2026-11-21, ifcjson.mjs): buildingSMART's draft JSON form, as IfcOpenShell's ifc2json (header, {"ref"} links, bare values) and IFC.JAVA (no header, every value wrapped, bare-id links, relationships nested under inverse attributes with the pointer back restored) write it; UUID GlobalIds become IFC's 22-character form; no header means the schema that knows the class names; id-less objects written at each use are one entity. On 97 STEP/ifcJSON twins in buildingSMART's ifcJSON repository: starter IDS verdicts 291 of 291 identical; with 65 public IDS, 6,552 of 6,596 same status and failing GlobalIds, every remaining difference a converter's omission (eval/ifcjson-twins-2026-11-21.md).
- IDS 1e-6 float tolerance; values converted to SI from project or property units; IFC2X3 occurrence classes via the type mapping table.
- bSDD links (2026-11-19, CLI `--audit SPEC.ids --bsdd`, bsdd.mjs): each facet uri is looked up in the buildingSMART Data Dictionary; errors for links bSDD lacks (names the IFC 4.3 entry), wrong kind, a dataType that cannot hold the dictionary's values; warnings for a baseName other than the linked property (names the baseName's own link), another IFC type, allowed values, classification system/code/related classes. On 58 public IDS files with 197 bSDD links: 7 with an error, 15 with a warning, all read by hand (eval/bsdd-links-2026-11-19.md). The only network call; not on the page (bSDD sends no CORS header).
- bSDD links written for you (2026-11-19, CLI `--link-bsdd SPEC.ids [-o OUT.ids]`, page "Download IDS with bSDD links", bsdd-suggest.mjs): offline; adds the IFC 4.3 dictionary uri (.../ifc/4.3/prop/<Name>) to requirement property facets on a standard Pset_/Qto_ property that have none, nothing else in the file changes. On 117 public IDS files: 617 links in 54 files, all of which resolve in bSDD (looked up live 2026-11-19; the 77 template names bSDD's IFC 4.3 dictionary lacks, Reference among them, are skipped; eval/bsdd-template-sweep.mjs checks all 760 sets: eval/bsdd-suggest-live-2026-11-19.md); on 212 facets already linking IFC, the same link 196 times, the 2 others author slips (eval/bsdd-suggest-2026-11-19.md).
- IDS from a bSDD class (2026-11-19, CLI `--from-bsdd CLASS_URI... [-o OUT.ids] [--sets A,B]`, bsdd-spec.mjs): one specification per bSDD class from its property list; entity (and classification) applicability, the class uri on a requirement classification, one property facet per class property with its bSDD uri, the IFC templates' dataType, allowed values or bounds, isRequired as cardinality; complex properties left out and said. On 185 classes from 42 bSDD dictionaries: 38 of 42 files audit clean (the rest repeat their dictionary's faults), 42 of 42 pass the bSDD link check (eval/bsdd-spec-2026-11-19.md). The editor keeps facet uris on open and write-back (0 of 344 public links before, 344 of 344 now). Measure types (2026-11-19, bsdd-units.mjs, schema/bsdd-units.json from bSDD's unit list and QUDT): a bSDD Real with a unit is written as the IFC measure it names (mm as IFCLENGTHMEASURE) with values and bounds in SI; dimensionless (%), unknown or conflicting units stay IFCREAL with a note; dB is written as IFCSOUNDPRESSURELEVELMEASURE or IFCSOUNDPOWERLEVELMEASURE when the property's physicalQuantity, name or ISO symbol says which (LA_Fmax_nT, L'nT,w pressure; L_W, LWA power; R_w, DnT,w stay IFCREAL; 2026-11-19, levelOf, eval/bsdd-db-2026-11-19.md, IfcTester 0.9.0 agrees 6 of 6 on a built wall class); bSDD's "°" link to QUDT GRAD (gon) is read as the degree. 867 of 1,625 Real properties outside IFC get a measure; on a built model the old IFCREAL facet failed a 200 mm IfcLengthMeasure wall and the new one passes it (IfcTester 0.9.0 agrees, 9 of 9) (eval/bsdd-units-2026-11-19.md).

## Not covered

- Geometry or clash checks (IDS does not specify them).

Results are a reading of the model against the IDS, not a design review or professional advice.
